question: Should the audio-capable yt-dlp fallback restriction apply to all generic transcription downloads, or remain Loom-specific until broader host compatibility is demonstrated?
rationale: The restriction is logically appropriate for transcription, but it changes a shared third-party format-selection policy whose cross-host compatibility cannot be settled by the focused Loom tests alone.

options.title: Validate and keep global
options.body: Test representative existing generic media hosts and keep the shared selector because video-only renditions cannot produce a transcript.

options.title: Scope to Loom
options.body: Preserve the prior selector for other hosts and apply the stricter fallback only to Loom to minimize upgrade risk.

recommendation.title: Validate and keep global
recommendation.body: Test representative existing generic media hosts and keep the shared selector because video-only renditions cannot produce a transcript.
